title: A term-insurance aggregator cut cost-per-qualified-lead 41% by buying comparison-intent search, not brand head terms
content: SITUATION: A Bengaluru term + health insurance aggregator spent ₹9.5L/month on Google, 70% on head terms like 'best term plan' at ₹480 CPC. Lead-to-qualified rate stuck at 11%, so cost per qualified lead (CPQL) hit ₹4,300. Trust was the wall: tier-2 buyers in Indore, Coimbatore and Jaipur abandoned the instant the form asked to 'share Aadhaar / income' — 63% drop-off there. ACTION: We moved 55% of Google budget off head terms onto high-intent long-tail ('LIC vs HDFC term plan 1 crore', 'term insurance for 35 year old non-smoker'), where CPC was ₹190. We built a no-login premium calculator showing 8 insurers side by side with their published IRDAI claim-settlement ratios, replaced forms with Click-to-WhatsApp ads on Meta (₹70 CPL) handing off to a human advisor, and ran 6 YouTube explainers on 'why claims get rejected' for men 30-45 at ₹0.40 CPV. OUTCOME: Over 90 days at flat spend, CPQL fell from ₹4,300 to ₹2,540 (-41%) and qualified-lead volume rose 2.3x. WhatsApp leads closed at 19% vs 9% for forms; comparison pages drove 38% of qualified pipeline. LESSON: Comparison-intent keywords convert ~2x better than brand head terms because the buyer is mid-decision, not browsing. When the blocker is trust, not information, a WhatsApp human handoff beats any form — spend down the long-tail funnel, not at the expensive top.
lesson: Comparison-intent keywords ('X vs Y plan') and a WhatsApp human handoff convert roughly 2x better than brand head terms and web forms, because the insurance buyer is mid-decision and the conversion blocker is trust, not information. Move spend down the long-tail funnel and replace the form with a human at the exact step where buyers stall.
